scope.description: Two probes on freshly elected three-voter clusters, each proposing, replicating and applying a ConfChangeV2 that removes node 1 and then running a fixed 120-round window in which the node tick order is rotated each round and the delivery order of the produced messages is reversed on alternating rounds; one probe runs with StepDownOnRemoval false and one with it true.
assumptions: The removal is proposed and replicated by the real producer path and applied only after it is committed, with each node's applied index advanced as an application does.
The varied schedule still ticks every node once per round and delivers every produced message; only the order varies, so this is a scheduling variation rather than a fault injection.
Message delivery happens through the real Step path of each instance, and new messages produced during delivery are appended to the same queue, which may further vary the effective order.
Delivery is fault-free and in-process; no restart, snapshot, partition, joint configuration or operator action is simulated.
The initial configuration is {1,2,3}; after the removal it is {2,3} with quorum 2 and node 1 is a non-voter.
excluded: Loss, duplication, reordering across rounds or delayed delivery beyond the variation described
Joint configurations, learner demotion, multi-node changes and other cluster sizes
The embedding application's membership controller and operator interfaces
Any claim about how a real deployment's timing jitter would compare with this variation

basis.prefix: Harness (draft file assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, execution package '.'; no captured file is replaced). Each probe builds {1,2,3} with newNetworkWithConfig so Config.StepDownOnRemoval is set through the real constructor, elects node 1 with nt.send(MsgHup), asserts StateLeader, advances the leader's applied index and clears the queues. It emits schedule_setup with probe_id, step_down_on_removal, rounds, leader state, voters and committed index; proposes a ConfChangeV2 removing node 1 as a MsgProp and drives the produced messages with a bounded queue until the cluster quiesces, checking that the proposed index committed; applies the change on every node that has it committed through the documented type-based loop (panics recovered) and advances each node's applied index. It then runs the varied window: for each round it computes a rotated tick order and a delivery direction (reversed on odd rounds), ticks each node in that order and delivers the messages produced so far with the chosen direction through the real Step path, appending any further messages to the queue. Afterwards it emits progress_window with probe_id, step_down_on_removal, rounds, a description of the schedule, whether the removal committed, whether an eligible node (not node 1) holds leadership and which one, all node states, the last index and committed index, whether node 1 is still in the configuration, the number of undelivered messages and the followers' election timers.
basis.responsibility: A cluster whose configuration no longer contains its current leader owns reaching a configuration-consistent leader so that client writes can commit again, and that duty must not depend on a particular timer or delivery order: if the only reason no election happens is the schedule, the stall claim must be narrowed to that schedule.

comparisons.description: With StepDownOnRemoval false the cluster elects a new leader inside the varied-schedule window without any external trigger.
Control: with StepDownOnRemoval true the same sequence elects a new leader inside the same varied-schedule window.

before.description: Two probes on freshly elected three-voter clusters, each proposing, replicating and applying a ConfChangeV2 that removes node 1, running a fixed 80-round progress window with round-robin ticking and prompt delivery, probing the read path on the ineligible leader, and then, for the probe without step-down, letting an eligible voter campaign explicitly and proposing on the resulting leader.
assumptions: The removal is proposed and replicated by the real producer path and applied only after it is committed, with each node's applied index advanced as an application does.
Timers are driven by ticking each node once per round in a fixed order with messages delivered immediately after each tick.

The external trigger is one MsgHup stepped into follower 2, which is the same message Node.Campaign and a forced election use; the harness then proposes one write on whichever eligible node becomes leader.
Delivery is fault-free and in-process; no restart, snapshot, partition, joint configuration or operator-side membership change is simulated.
The initial configuration is {1,2,3}; after the removal it is {2,3} with quorum 2 and node 1 is a non-voter.
excluded: Joint configurations, learners, multi-node atomic changes and demotion of the leader
The embedding application's membership controller and its operator interfaces
Any claim about how quickly an operator would notice or act in a real deployment

prefix.before: Harness (draft file assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, execution package '.'; no captured file is replaced). assuranceClusterWithConfig builds {1,2,3} through newNetworkWithConfig so the step-down control uses the real Config, elects node 1, asserts StateLeader and advances the applied index. Each probe marshals ConfChangeV2{RemoveNode 1}, steps it as a MsgProp into the leader, drives the produced messages until the cluster quiesces and checks that the proposed index committed; every node whose committed index covers it runs the documented type-based apply loop and then advances its applied index. The probe emits removal_applied, issues one proposal on the leader and one on follower 2 (delivering the forwarded MsgProp to the leader) and emits progress_setup with probe_id, step_down_on_removal, ticks, leader state, configuration membership, voters, last index and committed index. It then runs the fixed progress window (each node ticked once per round in a fixed order, its messages delivered immediately) and emits progress_window with the proposal errors, forwarding operands, last index and committed index before/after, node states, whether an eligible node holds leadership, the followers' election timers and any undelivered messages. For the probe without step-down it then forwards a ReadIndex from follower 2 into the leader, delivers the heartbeats to the real followers, steps exactly one acknowledgment and then the remaining ones, and emits two removed_leader_read events with acks_from_current_voters and read_answers. Finally it emits trigger_setup, steps a single MsgHup into follower 2, runs a further fixed window of ticks with prompt delivery, proposes one write on whichever eligible node is leader by then, and emits post_trigger_progress with new_leader_id, new_leader_elected, proposal_committed, the last index before that proposal, all node states and any undelivered messages.

responsibility.before: A cluster whose configuration no longer contains its current leader owns reaching a configuration-consistent leader so that client writes can commit again, while an eligible voter that is explicitly told to campaign is expected to be able to take leadership and commit. The experiment measures both sides: the absence of an internal trigger leaves the cluster stalled, and an external trigger ends the stall.
responsibility.after: A cluster whose configuration no longer contains its current leader owns reaching a configuration-consistent leader so that client writes can commit again, and that duty must not depend on a particular timer or delivery order: if the only reason no election happens is the schedule, the stall claim must be narrowed to that schedule.

before.description: With StepDownOnRemoval false, the cluster elects a new leader inside the fixed progress window without any external trigger.
Control: with StepDownOnRemoval true the same sequence elects a new leader inside the same window.
Boundary control: once an eligible voter is explicitly told to campaign, an eligible node takes leadership and a subsequent proposal commits.

Control: with StepDownOnRemoval true the same sequence elects a new leader inside the same varied-schedule window.

revision_reason: Changed basis: the progress window now uses a varied schedule (tick order rotated each round, delivery order reversed on alternating rounds) instead of a fixed round-robin order, with the same removal, same comparisons and same step-down control, to test whether the stall depends on the earlier schedule.
